key_insight: M^4World can generate realistic future driving scenes across multiple camera views and LiDAR at the same time, while letting users interactively control objects and keep the simulation stable for up to a minute. This makes driving-world generation more useful for realistic autonomous-driving simulation.
problem_solved: Existing driving world models often struggle with object-level controllability and long-horizon consistency. This paper addresses the need for a multimodal simulator that can both stay stable over long periods and support fine-grained interactive object manipulation.
method: Builds a multi-view, multimodal generative world model for driving scenes.
Synthesizes synchronized surround-view video streams and LiDAR scans for future timesteps.
Supports interactive object manipulation to change scene elements with fine-grained control.
Extends generation to minute-long streaming while aiming to preserve temporal stability.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a stronger foundation for autonomous-driving simulation, data augmentation, and closed-loop testing. It could improve training and evaluation of perception, prediction, and planning systems in more realistic and controllable virtual environments.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing inputs, world model, and outputs for multi-view video plus LiDAR.
A split-screen before/after example of interactive object manipulation in a driving scene.
A timeline visualization showing minute-long streaming stability over time.
A surround-view sensor layout icon set with synchronized camera and LiDAR streams.
paper_title: M$^\text{4}$World: A Multi-view Multimodal Driving World Model for Interactive Object Manipulation and Minute-long Streaming
paper_authors: Ke Cheng, Hanqiao Ye, Lei Shi, Yahui Liu, Yunhan Shen
